series_key: data label for time series mining
mechanism: Train pytorch-forecasting NBeats with stack_types=["trend","seasonality"] on labeled close series; dual residual blocks emit forecast and backcast; plot_interpretation splits the horizon into forced polynomial trend vs Fourier seasonality stacks so each bar’s path is attributed to regime-like components rather than a black-box residual.
data_needed: OHLC closes with time_idx/series ids; max_encoder_length (96–192); max_prediction_length (20–30); optional labeled trend markers from earlier series parts.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a neural sequence sensor whose outputs are explicitly trend vs seasonality regimes—usable as continuous structure features, not just a point forecast.
quote: The NBEATS model is unique in breaking down the forecasts into seasonality and trends (Of course, because these two are chosen in this article, the results can only be broken down into these two, but there can be many other combinations).

series_key: data label for time series mining
mechanism: Classify bar features for multi-horizon forecasting: open/high/low (and indicators like MACD/ADX/RSI) go in time_varying_unknown_reals when predicting several future bars because future OHLC is unknown at forecast time; only single-bar-ahead setups may promote them to time_varying_known_reals. Time-of-bar can be known_reals because the TF grid is fixed.
data_needed: Bar OHLC (+ optional indicators); TimeSeriesDataSet covariate lists; prediction_length>1 decision.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GOLD_micro M15; discussion generalizes to M15/H1/H4/D1 grids
why_new_for_mis: Codifies a MIS feature-typing rule for sequence models: multi-step horizons must treat concurrent bar features as unknown covariates, preventing leakage in regime/forecast sensors.
quote: if we want to predict the values of multiple bars? You may only know the data of the current bar, and the values behind are completely unknown, so it is not suitable for the environment discussed in our article, so we should add it to time_varying_unknown_reals.

series_key: data label for time series mining
mechanism: Export NBeats to ONNX; OnTimer every 300s CopyRates last 96 closes, z-score normalize into encoder_cont, pass mean/std as target_scale; OnnxRun yields prediction vector y[20]; if y.Mean() > (High[0]+Low[0])/2 set pre=buy else sell, then OnTick flips/opens a single position.
data_needed: NBeats.onnx resource; last 96 closes on chart symbol/period; High/Low of bar 0.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart _Symbol/_Period (trained on GOLD_micro M15; encoder=96, horizon=20)
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes a native-MT5 neural path-forecast sensor: multi-step mean vs current bar midpoint as a discrete directional change event without an external Python socket.
quote: if the mean of the predicted value is greater than the average of the highest and lowest values of the current bar, we assume that the future will be an upward trend, and set pre to “buy”, otherwise set pre to “sell”

why_new_for_mis: Exposes decomposable neural regime tensors inside the terminal—MIS can sense trend-stack vs seasonality-stack intensity live, not only a scalar buy/sell.

US=Winter & EU=Winter (USwinEUwin) = -7200

mechanism: Alongside offsets, store secFxWiWi/secFxSuSu/secFxSuWi (calendar seconds from week start to last Friday FX hour: typically 143h, 142h in US/EU interim). For any bar tB: tLeft = OffsetBroker.actSecFX - SoW(tB) yields hours left until FX close—session-liquidity countdown that shrinks through the week and jumps at DST change weekends.
data_needed: actSecFX for current DST regime; SoW(broker time); optional tGMT/tNY from actOffset.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 path simulation from history to TimeCurrent; multi-broker demo prints
why_new_for_mis: Turns FX week structure into a continuous liquidity/session sensor (time-to-close + DST-dependent week length) MIS can gate entries with.
quote: tLeft = OffsetBroker.actSecFX - SoW(arr1h[b]); // time till FX closes
